questions.prompt: A licensed Microsoft Entra tenant needs group membership to update automatically when a user’s department attribute becomes Finance. Which group configuration meets this requirement?
choices: A manually assigned security group with no automation
An Azure resource tag named Finance
A dynamic user group with a department-based membership rule
A device group based only on operating system
questions.explanation: A dynamic user membership rule evaluates supported user attributes. Resource tags and device rules do not evaluate user departments.
hints: Identify what evaluates user attributes and updates membership.

questions.prompt: An administrator must retrieve the built-in Contributor role definition for inspection before designing a custom role. Which PowerShell cmdlet retrieves that definition?
choices: Remove-AzRoleDefinition -Name "Contributor"
Get-AzResourceGroup -Name "Contributor"
Get-AzRoleDefinition -Name "Contributor"
Get-AzRoleAssignment -RoleDefinitionName "Contributor"
questions.explanation: Get-AzRoleDefinition retrieves the role’s permissions and scopes. Get-AzRoleAssignment retrieves grants of roles, not the definition itself. Export or serialization can then save the retrieved object.
hints: Distinguish a role definition from an assignment of that role.

questions.prompt: A VM cannot receive an expected TCP connection. You need to identify which effective security rule allows or denies the proposed source address, destination address and port. Which Network Watcher capability should you use?
choices: IP flow verify
A storage inventory report
Connection Monitor as a replacement for rule evaluation
A billing cost export
questions.explanation: IP flow verify evaluates the proposed TCP or UDP flow against applicable security rules and identifies the allowing or denying rule. It does not prove application health.
hints: Choose a security-rule evaluation tool rather than a long-term connectivity monitor.

questions.prompt: An application VM initiates TCP connections to an approved external service on destination port 8080. An NSG currently denies that outbound traffic. Which change addresses this requirement?
choices: Allow inbound TCP 8080 from every internet address
Add an appropriately scoped, higher-priority outbound allow rule for the service and TCP destination port 8080
Allow outbound UDP 8080 instead of TCP
Disable the NSG on every subnet
questions.explanation: The VM initiates the connection, so the relevant direction is outbound. The rule must match TCP, the destination and effective priority, while preserving other protections.
hints: Follow the initiating endpoint and the stated protocol.

questions.prompt: A regional application has three interchangeable VM replicas and must tolerate loss of one datacenter-scale availability zone. Which deployment most directly separates their zone failure domains?
choices: Put all replicas on one VM with more memory
Put all replicas in one zone with different names
Place replicas across three supported availability zones
Use one availability set and assume it spans three zones
questions.explanation: Availability zones provide separate datacenter-scale failure domains within a supported region. An availability set distributes fault and update domains but does not itself establish cross-zone placement.
hints: Match the required failure boundary to the deployment boundary.

questions.prompt: An administrator is evaluating supported Windows and Linux Azure VMs for backup. Which conclusion should guide the assessment?
choices: Azure VM Backup supports eligible Windows and Linux VMs; verify the support matrix and VM configuration
Operating system and configuration support never need checking
Any automatically shut down VM is always ineligible
Azure VM Backup supports only Windows VMs
questions.explanation: Azure VM Backup supports eligible Windows and Linux configurations. Disk, encryption, networking and other limits still need checking; an omitted table cannot establish eligibility for named machines.
hints: Distinguish broad OS support from the exact configuration support matrix.

questions.prompt: An operator has investigated a fired Azure Monitor alert and wants to record that someone is handling it without claiming that the monitored condition has resolved. Which field and value should be changed?
choices: Set the alert’s user response to Acknowledged
Force the monitor condition to Resolved
Change the resource’s region
Delete the alert instance
questions.explanation: User response tracks human handling with New, Acknowledged or Closed. Monitor condition reflects the monitored signal and is separate from the user’s handling state.
hints: Separate human handling status from the monitored condition.

questions.prompt: A storage account needs one alert for a management-plane deletion event and another for a capacity metric threshold. Which design matches these two different signal types?
choices: Use an activity-log rule to evaluate every numeric metric
Replace both alert rules with one email contact
Use a metric rule to evaluate every management operation
Use an activity-log alert rule and a metric alert rule
questions.explanation: Activity-log rules evaluate management events; metric rules evaluate numeric metrics. Notifications are configured through action groups rather than replacing signal evaluation.
hints: Identify the source and type of each signal.

questions.prompt: Two Azure Monitor alert rules must notify the same operations team by email. What reusable notification component can both rules reference?
choices: A custom DNS zone
An action group containing the required receivers
A VM availability set
A storage lifecycle policy
questions.explanation: An action group defines notification and action receivers and can be reused by alert rules. Exact receiver counts in the missing source table are not assumed.
hints: Choose the reusable alert notification component.

questions.prompt: A custom role should be assignable only within resource group rg-app in subscription 11111111-1111-1111-1111-111111111111. Which AssignableScopes entry identifies that group?
choices: /subscriptions/11111111-1111-1111-1111-111111111111/resourceGroups/rg-other
/subscriptions/22222222-2222-2222-2222-222222222222/resourceGroups/rg-app
/subscriptions/11111111-1111-1111-1111-111111111111/providers/Microsoft.Compute
/subscriptions/11111111-1111-1111-1111-111111111111/resourceGroups/rg-app
questions.explanation: A resource-group scope includes the subscription ID and resource-group name. A path ending at resourceGroups does not identify a concrete group.
hints: Look for the complete hierarchy ending in the named resource group.

questions.prompt: A custom role excludes an operation through NotActions. A user also holds another role that permits that operation at the same effective scope. What does the exclusion establish?
choices: It automatically deletes the other assignment
It blocks the operation from every role the user holds
It disables the resource provider
It subtracts the operation from the custom role; it is not an explicit deny against another role’s grant
questions.explanation: NotActions subtracts permissions from the role definition’s Actions. Other applicable role assignments can still grant the operation unless a separate deny mechanism applies.
hints: Distinguish subtraction from one grant from an explicit deny.

questions.prompt: A legacy design specifies a Basic Azure Load Balancer. The replacement must use a supported SKU with production features and explicit security rules. Which SKU is the appropriate general replacement?
choices: An availability set without a load balancer
Standard Load Balancer
A new Basic Load Balancer
A private DNS zone instead of load distribution
questions.explanation: Basic Load Balancer has retired. Standard is the supported migration destination; public IP compatibility, security rules and outbound design must also be reviewed.
hints: Select the supported successor and plan its associated networking requirements.

questions.prompt: VMs in two availability sets share the same supported virtual network configuration. They need one load balancer backend pool. Which Azure Load Balancer SKU supports this design?
choices: Azure Application Security Group
Standard Load Balancer
Azure DNS Private Resolver
Basic Load Balancer (retired)
questions.explanation: Standard Load Balancer supports backends across multiple availability sets. This question states its own supported network context rather than assuming the missing source VM table.
hints: Consider the supported backend placement capabilities of the SKU.

questions.prompt: Private VMs in subnet app need outbound internet connectivity without individual VM public IP addresses. A NAT gateway already has a public IP. Which association enables its use by those VMs?
choices: Attach its public IP as every VM’s private IP
Create an inbound NSG rule and omit the subnet association
Associate it only with an unrelated subnet called public
Associate the NAT gateway with subnet app
questions.explanation: NAT Gateway provides outbound connectivity for resources in its associated subnet. The subnet containing the workloads must use the gateway; naming another subnet public does not create a route through it.
hints: Locate the subnet containing the workloads that need outbound connectivity.

questions.prompt: Several compatible web apps run in the same region and operating-system family. Load tests show enough capacity in one App Service plan. Which design can share paid compute resources?
choices: Move the plan’s region on each incoming request
Mix incompatible operating-system plans into one app
Require one dedicated plan per app in every case
Host those compatible apps in the same appropriately sized plan
questions.explanation: Apps in an App Service plan share its compute resources. Capacity, OS, region, isolation and feature needs still matter; one plan is not universally the cheapest or safest design.
hints: Separate resource sharing from an unconditional cost guarantee.

questions.prompt: A network design uses Azure Virtual WAN and requires a regional virtual hub in each of three selected Azure regions. How should the hubs be organized?
choices: Replace the Virtual WAN with three storage queues
Create three regional virtual hubs within the Virtual WAN
Create an Azure availability set for each VPN site instead
Create one hub per physical datacenter regardless of design
questions.explanation: A Virtual WAN can contain multiple regional virtual hubs. Hub placement follows the regional network design; it is not inherently one hub per on-premises datacenter.
hints: Count required Azure hub regions rather than assuming a hub per branch.

questions.prompt: An AKS application must expose a supported public layer-4 endpoint for external clients. Which Kubernetes Service type requests an Azure load balancer frontend for that exposure?
choices: Headless Service
LoadBalancer Service
ClusterIP Service
ExternalName Service
questions.explanation: A LoadBalancer Service can request an externally accessible frontend unless configured as internal. ClusterIP serves cluster-internal access; endpoint exposure still needs security controls.
hints: Distinguish cluster-internal addressing from externally exposed service frontends.

questions.prompt: A deployment explicitly requires a Linux App Service plan in West Europe. Which existing plan is compatible with those stated plan requirements?
choices: A Windows plan in West Europe
A Windows plan in East US
A Linux plan in West Europe with sufficient capacity
A Linux plan in East US
questions.explanation: An App Service plan defines OS and region for its compute. Runtime support and capacity must be verified separately. The absent source plan table is not reconstructed.
hints: Check both the stated OS and the stated region.

questions.prompt: An administrator must manage Azure resource role assignments in one resource group without general permission to modify its workloads. Which listed built-in role is intended for access administration?
choices: User Access Administrator at the resource-group scope
Global Reader in Microsoft Entra ID
Reader at subscription scope
Contributor at subscription scope
questions.explanation: User Access Administrator manages Azure resource access. Contributor cannot create Azure RBAC role assignments; Entra directory roles are a different authorization system. Other access-management roles exist, so this asks among the listed roles.
hints: Separate access administration from general resource management.

questions.prompt: A user must create and manage subnets in an existing virtual network but does not need to assign roles. Which listed role should be scoped to that virtual network?
choices: User Administrator in the tenant
Network Contributor at the VNet
Reader at the VNet
Storage Blob Data Reader at the account
questions.explanation: Network Contributor manages network resources at its effective scope. Reader cannot modify resources; directory and blob-data roles do not grant subnet management.
hints: Match the resource provider and required operation.

questions.prompt: An App Service custom subdomain already has the required ownership verification record. You now need DNS to map www.example.com to appname.azurewebsites.net using an alias. Which record should be added?
choices: A TXT record as the only traffic-routing record
An NSG rule instead of a DNS record
A CNAME record for www pointing to appname.azurewebsites.net
An MX record for the web app
questions.explanation: A CNAME aliases the subdomain to the App Service hostname. Ownership verification is a separate step; an A record is another mapping method rather than an additional mandatory record here.
hints: Distinguish domain verification from alias-based name resolution.

questions.prompt: A supported Azure Files deployment must replicate synchronously across availability zones in one region. Which redundancy option directly meets that requirement?
choices: A VM snapshot as the storage-account redundancy setting
An unreplicated local disk
Zone-redundant storage (ZRS)
Locally redundant storage (LRS) alone
questions.explanation: ZRS synchronously replicates across availability zones in the primary region. Supported account types, regions and service options must be checked rather than assuming all premium shares support every redundancy choice.
hints: Match a zone-level resilience requirement to the redundancy option.

questions.prompt: Identity-based SMB authentication and share-level access are already configured for Azure Files. Finance users need read access to one directory and write access to another. Which additional mechanism provides directory-level granularity?
choices: A VM availability set
Storage-account Reader alone
The storage account’s display name
Windows directory and file ACLs
questions.explanation: Share-level permissions and directory/file ACLs serve different levels of access control. Windows ACLs provide the requested granular directory permissions.
hints: Identify the authorization layer below the share.

questions.prompt: An engineer must manage exactly two load balancers and has no need to manage any other resources in their resource group. Which scope choice best limits a suitable network-management role?
choices: Use a directory User Administrator role
Assign Owner to the entire subscription
Assign Contributor to every management group
Assign the role separately at each required load-balancer resource scope
questions.explanation: Resource-scoped assignments restrict the role to the selected load balancers and their child resources. Broader group or subscription scopes would grant unnecessary authority.
hints: Choose the narrowest scope matching the two named resources.

questions.prompt: An Azure VNet needs a site-to-site IPsec connection to an on-premises VPN appliance. Which Azure resource represents the on-premises gateway address and network prefixes?
choices: Public DNS zone
Azure Files share
Application security group
Local network gateway
questions.explanation: A local network gateway represents the on-premises VPN endpoint and address prefixes. A compatible virtual network gateway and connection resource are also required.
hints: Distinguish the representation of the remote site from the Azure-side VPN gateway.

questions.prompt: Operations needs an email when a VM management operation appears in the Azure Activity Log. Which combination evaluates the event and sends the notification?
choices: A storage lifecycle rule and a VM snapshot
An activity-log alert rule with an email action group
An NSG rule and an App Service plan
A metric chart with no alert rule or receiver
questions.explanation: The alert rule evaluates the management event; the action group supplies the notification receiver. A chart alone does not send a notification.
hints: Identify both the signal evaluator and notification receiver.

questions.prompt: A tenant’s external collaboration policy explicitly prevents a particular user role from inviting guests. A user in that role cannot invite a guest. Which configuration should the administrator review?
choices: The VNet subnet address range
The VM disk caching mode
Microsoft Entra external collaboration guest invitation settings
A blob lifecycle deletion policy
questions.explanation: External collaboration settings govern who can invite guests and permitted collaboration restrictions. A generic sign-in failure alone would not establish this specific policy cause.
hints: Use the stated policy evidence rather than diagnosing an unspecified error.

questions.prompt: An organization wants supported hybrid sign-in to validate passwords against on-premises Active Directory without synchronizing password hashes to Microsoft Entra ID. Which listed method matches that requirement?
choices: Password hash synchronization
A public storage account key
Pass-through authentication
Anonymous access
questions.explanation: Pass-through authentication validates credentials through on-premises agents. Availability and fallback design still matter; federation is another possible design, so it is not offered as an exclusive alternative.
hints: Locate where password validation happens in the requested design.

questions.prompt: A VM must allow RDP only from a specified on-premises prefix and continue serving HTTPS from the internet. The effective NSG currently allows both ports from anywhere. Which rule plan meets the requirement?
choices: Add an outbound RDP deny rule and keep inbound RDP open
Change the VNet address range without changing RDP rules
Deny all inbound internet traffic including HTTPS
Allow TCP 3389 from the approved prefix, deny other inbound TCP 3389 at a lower precedence, and preserve the HTTPS allow rule
questions.explanation: The permitted RDP source needs a higher-precedence allow, followed by a broader RDP deny. HTTPS remains independently allowed. Azure NSG rules evaluate lower priority numbers first.
hints: Trace inbound direction, destination port and rule precedence.
questions.evidence: Effective rules allow inbound TCP 3389 and 443 from any source.

questions.prompt: A VM will be created in West Europe using an existing VNet in West Europe. What placement must its network interface use?
choices: Any subnet in any region because names match
A subnet in that VNet, with the NIC in the VM’s region
An East US NIC connected directly to the West Europe VNet
A storage container instead of a subnet
questions.explanation: A NIC connects to a subnet in a VNet and is subject to regional placement requirements. The question states its own regions rather than recovering the missing source table.
hints: Check the NIC’s region and subnet relationship.

questions.prompt: A private application needs an internal frontend to distribute arbitrary TCP traffic to VMs. It does not need HTTP routing. Which service fits this layer-4 requirement?
choices: An internal Standard Load Balancer
A public DNS TXT record
A private storage queue
An application gateway solely because every protocol is HTTP
questions.explanation: Azure Load Balancer distributes supported layer-4 traffic. Application Gateway is designed for HTTP/HTTPS application delivery and should not be treated as a substitute for arbitrary TCP requirements.
hints: Match the required traffic layer and private exposure.

questions.prompt: Azure File Sync’s storage sync service and cloud endpoint already exist. The agent is installed on a supported Windows Server, but that server has not been registered. What should happen before creating its server endpoint?
choices: Register the server with the storage sync service
Create the endpoint while assuming an unregistered server is selectable
Convert the Azure file share into a blob container
Delete the cloud endpoint
questions.explanation: The server must be registered with the storage sync service before a server endpoint can bind its local path into the sync group. Agent installation alone is not registration.
hints: Identify the prerequisite between installing the agent and adding a server endpoint.

questions.prompt: A resource-group deployment needs a password stored in Key Vault. Review finds that the template author proposes checking a plaintext password into source control. Which replacement design best preserves the secret boundary?
choices: Rename the plaintext variable to secret without changing its contents
Commit the password and remove it after deployment
Use a secure template parameter with a Key Vault reference and configure the required deployment permissions
Grant every user vault administration to simplify deployment
questions.explanation: A Key Vault parameter reference keeps the secret value out of the checked-in parameter file. The vault and deployment principal must have the documented template-deployment permissions; secure parameter types avoid inappropriate exposure.
hints: Separate referencing a secret from copying its value into source control.
questions.evidence: The password is already held in Key Vault; the repository is broadly readable.
constraints: Do not store the plaintext secret in the repository

questions.prompt: A cost report identifies managed disks that appear unattached. What should an administrator do before deleting them?
choices: Assume unattached means no business value
Delete every disk whose name contains old
Verify disk state, ownership, retention needs and recovery dependencies, then obtain the appropriate disposal authorization
Delete the entire resource group without inspecting dependencies
questions.explanation: Unattached disks can contain needed data or retained recovery copies. Cost cleanup should verify state and business requirements before an authorized deletion.
hints: Separate a cleanup candidate from permission to destroy its contents.

questions.prompt: A policy must require MFA for sign-ins from outside specified trusted named locations. Which Conditional Access condition directly represents that location requirement?
choices: A storage replication setting
A VM update domain
A sign-in-risk condition as an exact substitute for location
Network/location conditions using the configured named locations
questions.explanation: Named locations support location-based Conditional Access. Sign-in risk measures detected risk and is a different signal; geographic location is not itself a risk score.
hints: Choose the condition that directly represents the stated signal.

questions.prompt: A correctly scoped Azure Policy assignment denies creation of Microsoft.Compute/virtualMachines. An authorized Contributor’s new VM deployment fails with a policy violation. Which explanation is most appropriate?
choices: Role permissions do not bypass the effective deny policy
The VM name must match the user’s display name
Contributor always overrides policy denies
A Reader role would bypass the same deny
questions.explanation: RBAC permissions authorize actions but do not override an applicable policy deny. Any needed exception must follow the organization’s policy and exemption process.
hints: Separate action authorization from policy compliance.

questions.prompt: An event must be made available independently to billing and shipping consumers. Each consumer needs its own copy of matching messages. Which Service Bus entity design supports this?
choices: An NSG with two inbound rules
One storage table with no message subscriptions
One queue where the consumers compete for the same messages
A topic with separate subscriptions for billing and shipping
questions.explanation: Service Bus topics support publish-subscribe through subscriptions. Each subscription receives matching messages and has independent consumption.
hints: Distinguish independent subscriptions from competing queue consumers.

questions.prompt: Several workers should share work from one Service Bus queue. After a worker completes a message successfully, it should not also be processed as independent work by every worker. Which model fits?
choices: A separate topic subscription for every worker when all copies must be processed
Competing consumers with correct settlement and duplicate-safe processing
Sending the same message independently to every worker
A guarantee that failures can never redeliver a queue message
questions.explanation: Queue workers compete for messages. Locks, failures and retries can cause redelivery, so handlers still need appropriate settlement and idempotency.
hints: Distinguish work sharing from broadcast and from an exactly-once guarantee.

questions.prompt: You have an ARM template intended for resource-group scope and an existing group rg-app. Which Azure CLI command family targets that group’s deployment?
choices: az deployment group create --resource-group rg-app
az account clear
az deployment tenant create --resource-group rg-app
az group delete --name rg-app
questions.explanation: az deployment group create performs resource-group-scoped deployments. Subscription, management-group and tenant scopes use different commands and templates.
hints: Match the template’s declared scope to the deployment command.

questions.prompt: A team wants to delete a resource group containing a Recovery Services vault. Review discovers protected backup items and retained soft-deleted recovery data. What is the safest next step?
choices: Disable all recovery safeguards solely to make deletion convenient
Force-delete the vault without reviewing recovery data
Inventory vault dependencies and retention protections, preserve required recovery data, and follow the documented authorized cleanup sequence
Assume stopping one backup schedule removes all vault dependencies
questions.explanation: Vault removal requires resolving its actual dependencies and recovery protections. Stopping future backups alone does not remove retained items; cleanup must respect authorization and retention requirements.
hints: Separate stopping future protection from disposing of existing recovery data.
questions.evidence: The vault still contains protected items and soft-deleted recovery data.

questions.prompt: An authenticated administrator with sufficient blob permissions needs to create a container named vmimages in storage account exampleaccount using AzCopy. Which command uses the correct public Azure Blob endpoint?
choices: azcopy make "https://exampleaccount.blob.core.windows.net/vmimages"
azcopy make "https://vmimages.file.core.windows.net/exampleaccount"
azcopy remove "https://exampleaccount.blob.core.windows.net/vmimages"
azcopy make "https://exampleaccount.images.core.windows.net/vmimages"
questions.explanation: AzCopy make can create a blob container at the account’s blob endpoint. The images.core.windows.net host is not the standard Azure Blob service endpoint; remove performs a different operation.
hints: Check both the operation and the service endpoint.

questions.prompt: A Windows Server directory needs to synchronize through Azure File Sync. Which cloud storage resource is the sync group’s cloud endpoint based on?
choices: An Azure file share
A blob container
An Azure managed disk
A Service Bus queue
questions.explanation: Azure File Sync synchronizes server endpoints with an Azure Files cloud endpoint. Other storage services are not interchangeable cloud endpoints for this feature.
hints: Choose the cloud storage service used by Azure File Sync.

questions.prompt: An application identity needs to read, write and delete blob data in one container. General management-plane Contributor is insufficient for its Microsoft Entra-authorized data requests. Which listed role supplies the requested data access?
choices: Microsoft Entra User Administrator
Reader at subscription scope
Network Contributor
Storage Blob Data Contributor at the container scope
questions.explanation: Storage Blob Data Contributor grants blob data operations at the effective scope. General management-plane roles do not automatically grant this identity-based blob data access.
hints: Distinguish storage management permissions from blob data permissions.

questions.prompt: A supported internal Standard Load Balancer design must distribute TCP and UDP flows across all ports to a network appliance backend. Which rule feature is designed for this requirement?
choices: A single HTTPS-only rule
An App Service deployment slot
A CNAME record
High availability ports
questions.explanation: An HA ports rule on an internal Standard Load Balancer supports all-port TCP/UDP flow balancing. Frontend, backend, health and appliance forwarding configuration still need to be correct.
hints: Match an all-port layer-4 requirement to the specialized rule feature.

questions.prompt: An ARM template defines a location parameter but hardcodes each resource’s location. A deployment overrides the parameter and the resources remain in the hardcoded region. What corrects the mismatch?
choices: Set each intended resource’s location property to the location parameter expression
Use an unused tag named location
Rename the resource without changing its location expression
Delete all parameters and rely on the resource name
questions.explanation: A parameter only affects properties that reference it. A resource location expression such as [parameters('location')] must use a valid Azure location identifier and a supported service region.
hints: Trace whether the resource property actually references the overridden parameter.

questions.prompt: An Azure Load Balancer design explicitly requires a three-tuple session hash using source IP, destination IP and protocol. Which session persistence option matches those fields?
choices: Round robin by user display name
Client IP and protocol
None: five-tuple distribution
Client IP: two-tuple distribution
questions.explanation: Client IP and protocol uses the three-tuple distribution mode. Client IP uses two tuples; the default includes source and destination ports in a five-tuple hash.
hints: Count the fields in the required session key.

questions.prompt: A staff member must create and manage users in a specific Microsoft Entra tenant, without general subscription resource administration. Which listed directory role fits?
choices: Contributor on an Azure VM
User Administrator in that tenant
Network Contributor on a VNet
Storage Blob Data Contributor on a container
questions.explanation: User Administrator is a Microsoft Entra directory role. Azure resource roles grant permissions over resources, not general directory user administration, and roles in another tenant do not transfer automatically.
hints: Distinguish directory administration from Azure resource administration.

questions.prompt: A Linux VM needs supported Azure Monitor collection of guest syslog and performance counters. Which agent-based design should replace a retired diagnostics-extension approach?
choices: Azure Monitor Agent with an appropriate data collection rule
A VM size change without data collection
An activity-log alert as the only collector of guest syslog
A new deployment of the retired Linux Diagnostics extension as the default
questions.explanation: Azure Monitor Agent and data collection rules configure supported guest telemetry collection and destinations. The retired diagnostics extension is not the default for a new deployment.
hints: Separate guest data collection from Azure management-plane events.

questions.prompt: A network team needs ongoing reachability and latency checks from selected VM sources to specified destination endpoints. Which Network Watcher feature fits these active tests?
choices: A storage lifecycle policy
An inventory of every packet from every connection
Connection Monitor
A role assignment export
questions.explanation: Connection Monitor tests configured endpoints and reports connectivity and performance. It is not a capture of every packet or a complete inventory of all ambient traffic.
hints: Choose active tests between selected endpoints rather than blanket traffic capture.

questions.prompt: A VM must send selected guest events to Log Analytics and notify operators when a query detects an error pattern. Which complete chain addresses collection, evaluation and notification?
choices: Azure Monitor Agent plus an associated data collection rule, the workspace, a log alert rule and an action group
A workspace without any ingestion source
An NSG rule and a public IP address
An agent installation alone with no collection rule or alert
questions.explanation: AMA and an associated DCR collect selected data to the destination. A log alert evaluates a query and an action group delivers notifications. Each stage must be configured and verified.
hints: Trace the signal from collection through evaluation to notification.
questions.evidence: The VM has no configured guest-log collection and the operators require query-based detection.
constraints: Collect only the required guest events
Use Log Analytics for the query

questions.prompt: An operator has Virtual Machine Contributor and can manage a VM. They also need to grant someone else an Azure RBAC role. Does their existing VM role alone authorize that grant?
choices: Yes; guest administrator access automatically grants directory administration
No; it does not grant Azure RBAC role-assignment administration
Yes; every VM management role can assign all roles
Yes; VM power control implies subscription ownership
questions.explanation: Virtual Machine Contributor manages VM operations but does not permit Azure RBAC role assignments. Guest OS access, resource management and directory roles are different boundaries.
hints: Separate managing the VM from managing Azure access to it.

questions.prompt: A supported client mounts an Azure Files SMB share through its normal SMB endpoint. Which outbound TCP port must the network allow for that SMB traffic?
questions.explanation: SMB uses TCP 445 for this access path. Authentication, DNS and storage network restrictions still need to be configured separately.
hints: Identify the protocol used by the file share.

questions.prompt: A supported VM scale set rolling-upgrade policy limits each batch to 20% of a 20-instance set. Ignoring rounding because the result is an integer, how many instances can be in one upgrade batch?
questions.explanation: 20% of 20 is 4. This policy calculation does not promise that the other 16 instances are all healthy; health checks and unhealthy-instance limits must be configured independently.
hints: Apply the stated batch percentage; avoid inferring a health guarantee.

questions.prompt: An NSG rule references an application security group, and a VM’s traffic should be represented by that group. What resource configuration supplies the VM’s membership?
choices: Assign a Microsoft Entra user to the VM’s guest OS
Add the VM’s display name to a DNS TXT record
Associate the relevant NIC IP configuration with the application security group
Add a storage tag with the group’s name
questions.explanation: Application security group membership is configured on relevant network interface IP configurations, subject to supported VNet constraints. It is not directory group membership.
hints: Locate the network configuration that participates in the NSG match.

questions.prompt: A workload subnet must send traffic for a specified remote prefix through a network virtual appliance at a known private IP. Which user-defined route next-hop type represents that appliance?
choices: Internet
Virtual appliance
None
Virtual network
questions.explanation: Virtual appliance forwards matching traffic to the configured NVA private IP. The route must be applied at the appropriate source subnet, and appliance forwarding must be enabled.
hints: Match an explicit intermediary IP address to the next-hop type.

questions.prompt: A route table on the source subnet sends a remote prefix to an NVA’s private IP. The NIC does not permit IP forwarding and the appliance OS is not configured to forward. What should be corrected before treating the route as functional?
choices: Delete the source subnet’s route-table association
Grant the application a directory user role
Enable the required NIC IP forwarding and configure forwarding in the appliance OS
Change the route’s next hop to None
questions.explanation: Azure NIC IP forwarding and the appliance’s own forwarding behavior must both permit transit traffic. A route pointing to an NVA does not by itself turn the VM into a router.
hints: Check both Azure’s interface setting and the appliance’s own forwarding path.
questions.evidence: The route points to the appliance but both forwarding layers are disabled.

routing.note: The current app has a generic AZURE category, not an AZ_104 enum. Use a dedicated AZ-104 pool; do not publish into AZ-900.
